root_cause: The Scrape native driver used the shared sidepanel harness but did not read the live resource guard journal, lease owner, or stop marker before UI action batches. Its wrapper could record an unsafe watchdog sample while the driver continued and recorded later observations.
source_change: The shared native harness exposes a guard-owned resource health check and action wrapper. Scrape checks at batch starts and after long waits before accepting observations. The reader requires the current run and owner token, an admitted pending journal, a healthy or admitted sample no older than the policy watch interval, and no unsafe or stop evidence.
policy_unchanged: The existing resource-policy.json floors, watch interval, and sustained watchdog stop behavior were not edited.

lightweight_evidence.file_backed_test: node --test tests/browser/native-resource-boundary.test.mjs: 1 passed; fresh healthy and guard recovery metadata permitted, unsafe/stale/wrong-run/stop/missing-journal refused; delayed journal read advancing the clock across the watch interval refuses the action; refused reload cannot record a start
lightweight_evidence.mutants: Scratch-copy constant-healthy and early-clock mutations each made the test fail (exit 1); working source was not mutated.
lightweight_evidence.syntax: node --check passed for the native harness and Scrape driver

remaining: No native browser, build, or release run was authorized in this lane. A fresh peer must review source, then the run owner must obtain guarded native evidence on an exact artifact before any product acceptance claim.
